title: Ahu Tongariki, Rapa Nui
summary: Ahu Tongariki on Rapa Nui (Easter Island) is a ceremonial platform whose central part is close to 100 m long and carries 15 moai, the largest 14 m high with its topknot. The statues were toppled in the island's wars, then scattered by a tsunami after the Valdivia earthquake on 20 May 1960. A University of Chile team restored the ahu in 1992–1995 with funds from a Japanese company.

uncertainty.note: No page opened dates the ahu itself. A 1993 ABC piece says it was constructed 'a thousand years ago', so 993 is that phrase counted back from 1993, with a wide margin. UNESCO/ICOMOS dates the island's moai and ahu tradition only to between the 10th and 16th centuries. End is the present.

phases.description: Built about a thousand years before 1993 (ABC); the standing statues were later thrown down in the island's wars (CNCR dates that 'Huri Moai' phase to the 17th to 19th centuries, which is why this phase ends at 1600). The ahu's own building date is not in the sources.

Almost all the statues were toppled from their platforms in the Huri Moai phase, many broken (CNCR); on 20 May 1960 a wave after the Valdivia earthquake scattered the remains over about 4 hectares (CNCR; ABC).
Rebuilt by a multidisciplinary team led by the University of Chile with funds and a large crane from a Japanese company (CNCR).
Standing, with consolidation and hydrophobic treatment of the moai carried out by CNCR with the Nara conservation institute under a UNESCO project in 2004 (CNCR).

materials.material: volcanic tuff (CNCR treats the moai as volcanic tuff)

reviewer_note: Shape statue_group with a moai count of 15, as briefed. The building date is the weakest claim: no page opened dates the ahu, so start 993 rests on a 1993 broadcast phrase ('a thousand years ago') and the 1600 end of the first phase on CNCR's '17th to 19th centuries' Huri Moai period. CNCR gives restoration as 1992-1995; other pages seen say 1996. The 4-hectare scatter is from the ABC piece. The OSM point is the only coordinate source (the UNESCO point for Rapa Nui National Park is a whole-park centre, not Tongariki). The CNCR height is for the largest statue with its topknot; the tuff material is not stated for Tongariki by CNCR, so check or drop it.
